subject: Development has happened, so you have no right to complain
alt: Rajendra Dhodapkar's cartoon: on the left stands a plump, cheerful politician in glasses and a saffron shawl, a sheet of paper in his hand. Smiling, he says: '...according to our figures your development has already happened, so you people have no right to complain or make demands.' On the right stand four people: a thin man in a white vest and dhoti, hand outstretched, trying to say something; behind him a man in a white kurta-pyjama with an angry face; then a man in a blue shirt; and at the end a woman in a green saree. All four look tired and resentful. Behind them are the outlines of huts and broken houses. The cartoonist's signature is at the bottom left.
chutki: The figures on the paper say development has happened, and the politician is waving that paper to announce that people now have no right to complain. The faces of the four standing before him say something else: for those whose homes stand broken in the lines behind, whose hands are empty, development has happened on paper, not on the ground.

Dhodapkar's note is on the gap between official figures and life on the ground, a gap that is often erased by saying 'development has happened' instead of filling it. The sharpest part of the cartoon is that the politician is smiling and the crowd stands silent, as if the very permission to complain has been taken away.
